newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks give up gains after U.S. GDP data.
newsitem.headline: French stocks give up gains after U.S. GDP data.

text.p: French stocks gave up their gains after stronger than expected U.S. first-quarter GDP data showing the economy grew at the fastest pace in more than nine years.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was up 2.42 points, or 0.09 percent, at 2,605.28 at 1305 GMT, while the CAC-40 futures contract was up one point at 2,606.
The CAC had risen as high as 2,626.84 earlier.
U.S. first-quarter GDP growth came in at 5.6 percent, at an annualised rate, against expectations of 4.1 percent growth, fuelling inflation fears.
The GDP data proved a cold shower after Tuesday's economic data which dampened inflation fears and cause a rally on Wall Street with a 2.6 percent gain.

* Rhone-Poukenc held a five percent gain at 197.40 francs on the back of its 1997 first quarter profit and its maintaining a forecast of a 20 percent rise in the full year earnings per share, despite a setback at the Centeon joint venture for a product recall.
